diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proofs of \cref{thm:CK21thm3} and \cref{thm:UCSthm4.2} differ by a single step, namely the calculation of an infinite geometric progression

issues.failure_explanation: The even-index geometric progression requires cancellation of odd contributions to the integration error, not merely symmetric node locations. For example, the probability measure (1/4)delta_{-1}+(1/3)delta_{-1/2}+(5/12)delta_1 has one-point Gaussian node 0, but its integral of t^3 is 1/8 while the quadrature gives zero. Thus even symmetric nodes and weights do not make the underlying integration functional even. The theorem supplies no measure-symmetry hypothesis, and the paper gives no alternative argument establishing its sharper constant under the advertised node-only condition.

issues.failure_explanation: The objective treats a possibly negative real lower bound on m as an actual iteration cost. Admissible choices n=2, lambda_min=0.49, lambda_max=0.5 and epsilon=0.5 give C approximately 0.00396.
